summary: Kansas rallied past Baylor 25-24 behind Edwards and a late blocked field goal. Fourth-down execution now meets a demanding TCU defense, with Saturday’s kickoff set for 2:30 p.m. CT.

items.headline: Herold’s blocked field goal seals a 25-24 win
items.tldr: Kansas scored 15 fourth-quarter points to beat Baylor. The next step is to make earlier possessions count before another finish demands a special-teams rescue.

items.headline: Kansas converts five of eight fourth-down attempts
items.tldr: KU Sports details how formation and timing helped keep drives alive. Watch the alignment before the snap as closely as the final yard gained.

items.headline: Edwards carries 30 times for 156 yards
items.tldr: The running back gave Kansas a dependable way to move the chains. Watch whether the line can create the same first crease against TCU.

items.headline: The Kansas State loss remains a run-defense warning
items.tldr: Kansas allowed 359 rushing yards in the October 17 game. Keep the lesson dated to that outing: hold the edge and close the cutback before pursuing the next tackle.

items.headline: Kansas visits TCU at 2:30 p.m. CT on FS1
items.tldr: The Horned Frogs’ defense leads the Big 12 in yards allowed per game, according to Kansas’s preview. Expect sustained execution to matter more than one surprise call.

lead.headline: Earn the next manageable down.
lead.body: Make the first carry and the quick completion useful before reaching fourth down. Carry that discipline to defense: close the cutback lane and tackle through the runner’s hips.

matchup.thesis: Keep the offense ahead of the decision
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Build a drive that leaves a real choice on the next down. Use formation and tempo deliberately, with the line and quarterback aligned on the same answer.

signals.title: Backfield workload and early-down rushing
signals.summary: Make the carries sustain the drive
signals.detail: Watch the first block and Edwards’s path through the crease. Judge the workload by whether the next carry remains useful when the defense narrows the inside lane.

signals.title: Fourth-down operation
signals.summary: Make the alignment part of the call
signals.detail: Get the formation, snap and blocking assignment settled before the ball moves. Aggression only helps when every player is executing the same play.

signals.title: Run-defense fits
signals.summary: Close the lane behind the first tackle
signals.detail: Hold the edge while the inside pursuit closes the cutback. Do not let a failed first tackle turn the whole defense toward the wrong gap.

signals.title: Scoring possessions
signals.detail: Take the clean completion and protect the ball through contact. Make the red-zone call serve the available space rather than the hoped-for highlight.
